Home
Right at the heart of Aldro life is a supportive and caring community. From the day you arrive, as a pupil, parent or member of staff, you are welcomed into the Aldro family and that sense of community and belonging far outlasts one's time at the school.
Our children are inspired by passionate and enthusiastic staff who ensure they are nurtured, challenged, and fulfilled in equal measure. We are proud of our proven reputation of sending children to academically selective senior schools and achieving a high number of scholarships each year
With small numbers, Aldro never feels overwhelming. More like a small village where everyone knows you.
Our broad curriculum is carefully designed to provide academic rigour alongside exceptional opportunities in the arts, creativity, and sport.
Children discover what it feels like to belong to a family that stretches beyond their own.
We're independent which means we are not tied to a single senior school destination. Children leave us for a wide constellation of senior schools each chosen to suit their spark.
A guiding Aldro principle: nurturing curiosity, independence, resilience, and the joy of learning.

Headmaster's Welcome
Welcome to the Aldro website and thank you for your interest. I hope that what you find here will give you a good insight into all that Aldro has to offer.
Aldro is a coeducational day and boarding school for approximately 200 children aged between 7 and 13. Nestled in the quintessentially English and very beautiful village of Shackleford, Aldro lies just 30 miles southwest of London and is in easy reach of both Heathrow and Gatwick airports. With our full, weekly and family-friendly boarding, Aldro welcomes children from all around the world, as well as those looking for an idyllic country education away from the capital and many who join us daily from the towns and villages surrounding our stunning rural location in the home county of Surrey.
At Aldro, we are proud of our long history and proven success in preparing young people to attend leading independent senior schools, yet despite our heritage and traditions, our aim is to offer a modern, progressive and innovative curriculum that will prepare both girls and boys for their personal and professional lives beyond school.
Life at Aldro is also lots of fun. As you walk around the grounds, you will see children playing a whole variety of sports, rowing on the lake, learning the rules of Pétanque, or playing pirates on our very own adventure island. You will see them rehearsing for an upcoming play, singing in the choir, or heading off to the woods for yet another outdoor education lesson. Aldro life is guaranteed to be varied and stimulating!
Our small class sizes and high aspirations ensure that Aldro pupils achieve their very best in the classroom. We want them to discover a love of learning that will stay with them for life. Many will move on from Aldro to the UK’s top independent senior schools, often with scholarships and awards that reflect the diversity and excellence of their achievements along the way.
If children are to thrive at school, they must first feel happy. Our strong pastoral model and tangible sense of community, together with the values that stem from our Christian foundation, underpin our day-to-day lives here, helping to ensure that each child is uniquely known and individually valued. Our communal life is characterised by core values such as kindness, respect and integrity, and the school’s Christian foundation is as important today as it ever was; our lively Chapel services and engaging Assemblies begin each day and help to provide focus and context for the learning that follows. Aldro parents also contribute much to our sense of community and, when your child joins Aldro, you too become a part of the wider Aldro family.
We very much hope that, having visited our website, you will choose to visit Aldro in person. If you do so, Nicky and I shall be delighted to welcome you; we look forward to showing you around Aldro, the special place that is both our school and home.
Mr Chris Carlier
Headmaster

History of Aldro
“ELB” (whose portrait hangs over the fireplace in the drawing room at Aldro) decided to get his younger brother Harold to start up an annexe which Harold decided to name “Aldro” after a farm in Yorkshire that he regularly visited. The name simply means alder row or row of alder trees.
In September of 1898 Aldro moved over the road to what is still known as Aldro House in Darley Road, Eastbourne. Today it is a part of the University of Brighton.
Aldro began with just 36 boys who paid 100 guineas a year in fees and from the start they adopted the Browne family crest with its motto of “Suivez Raison” (follow the right).
The Rev Harold Browne was a remarkable man and under his leadership the school appears to have been a happy place. All the boys were boarders and they came from all over the country with very few coming from Sussex.
The First World War was to cost 37 old boys their lives and this terrible loss is remembered each year on a school trip to the battlefields of the Western Front as well as in the school chapel on Remembrance Day.
By the late summer of 1922 Rev Harold Browne was becoming ill and he died on 13th September 1922. His brother Charles took over briefly for two terms, but by the summer of 1923 it was decided to sell the school. The new Headmaster was Frederick Hill who had been wounded at Gallipoli in the First World War and, when the war ended, made the decision to go into education.
Frederick Hill and his wife Audrey dramatically changed the school. Houses were introduced called “Squads”, because the boys would do a few minutes military drill each day. They were named after the countries of the Empire and it was not until 1978 that drill ceased to be part of the school day.
New sports like rugby and hockey were introduced, as was boxing, which again continued until the late 1970s.
The years of the Depression from 1929 were hard times and at one point numbers fell to just 33. Frederick and Audrey worked tirelessly and they were fortunate that such a loyal staff stayed with them.
1939 saw the start of the Second World War and by the summer of 1940 Britain was facing the threat of invasion with the Battle of Britain raging in the skies above Kent and Sussex.
All schools had to evacuate from Eastbourne and by pure good fortune Hall Place in Shackleford became available in 1940. The owner, Sir Edgar Horne, had recently lost his wife and he wished to sell the property. After his death in 1941 the school would purchase Hall Place for £10,000 in 1942.
Life in wartime Shackleford was not easy with the playing fields being used to grow hay, and often the boys helped on local farms alongside the Italian POW’s from the camp, at what is now Rose Cottage.
World War II cost 20 Old Aldronians their lives and so in 1949 the barn was converted into the “War Memorial Chapel” as a permanent memorial to all those who had made the supreme sacrifice. As Britain slowly recovered from the war so Aldro began to grow, but the years of strain had taken their toll on Frederick Hill and on 28th October 1952 he died. His elder son Crispin had been teaching at Winchester after war service in the Navy, and he took over the role of Headmaster.
Crispin was a gifted teacher and under his leadership the school grew to 140 boys by the time he retired in 1984. Education to Crispin was not just something that happened in the classroom and he loved practical tasks such as building bridges over the lake with the boys on a Sunday. He was also ahead of many other educational thinkers when it came to special needs teaching, and after his retirement in 1984 he was to set up “Skillway” in Godalming to help young people who had problems with main stream education.
The first dayboys started during the war and by the time Crispin retired there were far more dayboys than boarders, with the vast majority of pupils coming from a 15 mile radius of the school.
From 1954 to 1964 Aldro had its own pre-prep department in the old Italian POW camp buildings on the site of Rose Cottage, but after the teacher in charge became ill in 1963 it was decided to close it and the land was sold for development.
Crispin Hill retired in July 1984 and Aldro had its fourth Headmaster, Ian Argyle. Ian and Jo Argyle set about transforming the school. They worked very hard to promote the school in the local area and new money made it possible to set about some ambitious building projects, the first of which being the swimming pool, resulting in the boys no longer having to swim in the lake, although the school still uses the lake for rowing. A new multi-purpose hall named after Crispin Hill was opened in 1987, new DT and Science departments followed as well as an Art room. For the centenary of the school in 1998 a whole new teaching block with changing rooms for sport was constructed and Aldro became a thoroughly modern school.
In the summer of 2001, after 17 years, Ian and Jo Argyle retired, and the reins were handed over to David and Sue Aston. They spent the next fourteen years filling the school and building a legacy of academic scholarship and all-round excellence. The school has also seen considerable success through chess, shooting and huge numbers of model railway enthusiasts. Their passion for music and the performing arts has seen record numbers of boys taking part in concerts, performances and music lessons. Development pace didn't slow down much, and the school was delighted to welcome the Earl of Wessex to open the new Aston Sports Centre in June 2015, just before David and Sue's retirement. The summer of 2015 saw the handover from the Astons to James and Jenny Hanson. James stepped down as Headmaster on health grounds in 2018 and following a year when Chris Rose, Deputy Head for over ten years, ably served as Acting Headmaster. Chris Carlier was appointed Aldro's new Headmaster from September 2019.
The War Memorial Chapel
The chapel was originally built as a barn around 1806 when Lord Midleton of Peperharow bought this estate. You can still see where the great doors were on either side of the building; one side is now the organ loft but the curved beam that once was over the doors on the other side is clearly visible. These doors allowed air flow through so that men threshing grain in the main part of the barn could have the chaff blown away and so they would only be left with the ears of wheat which could then be swept up and put into sacks.
When Sir Edgar Horne took over Hall Place in 1894 he used the barn as his garage. In 1940 Aldro relocated to its present site and the barn was still used as a garage until 1949 when it was turned into "The War Memorial Chapel". Bishop Reindorp (Bishop of Guildford) took the service when it was dedicated to the fifty-seven Aldro boys who gave their lives in both World War I and World War II.
Frederick Earnest Hill (FEH) bequeathed an organ which still remains in the chapel and dates from 1785 and many of the pews in the Chapel were given by Old Aldronians.
The War Memorial Chapel is where the Aldro community gathers together for a daily act of worship, providing the school with a meeting place and a start to the working day. Our simple act of worship always includes a hymn, reading and prayer, as well as a homily, offering a thought for the day applicable to the whole community.
As a school we are very proud of our strong choral tradition and our chapel choir adds a different spiritual dimension to our worship. We welcome visiting preachers at these services many of whom are drawn from senior public schools. Pupils take an active part in all our services.
Aldro Celebrated 75 Years in Shackleford 1940-2015
In 2015 Aldro celebrated 75 years since the school moved from its original home in Eastbourne to Shackleford. To commemorate we produced a book written by Nick Swan and Lizzie Geffen. Nick was the Head of History at Aldro for over 30 years and is the school archivist having maintained and developed the Aldro museum in the Cyder Press.
Lizzie Geffen is married to an OA, James (1970-75) and is the mother of Freddie and Tom who were both at Aldro at the time of writing. The foreword was written by Robert Stovold, a previous President of The Old Aldronian Association. He was also one of the first boys to join the school at its new home in Shackleford in 1940.
Copies of Aldro 75 Years in Shackleford are available from the School Secretary at Aldro and cost £20.

Breakages:
Where pupils are responsible for damage or breakage of school property as a result of misbehaviour or ill-treatment, replacement or repair charges, plus labour where applicable, will appear on the fee bill. Parents will be notified of llarger commitments.
Deposit:
A deposit of £1,000 for UK permanent residents or £11,000 for international pupils* and full boarders is payable with the completion of the Acceptance form (VAT is not applicable). The deposit is refundable after the payment of the final invoice at Aldro (less any outstanding charges) or if a pupil leaves giving one term’s notice but is otherwise non-refundable. The deposit will be forfeited if the pupil subsequently fails to take up the place for whatever reason.
*International pupils are deemed as those children either, whose main residence is not in the UK, are a non-UK passport holder or requiring Confirmation of Acceptance of Studies sponsorship.
Fees in advance
The fees in advance scheme requires a minimum of at least two years’ (6 terms) fees in advance, and increments of one year’s fees thereafter, up to the maximum six years (18 terms) at Aldro. The discount rate for the Scheme is set by the Governors each year and the scheme year is 1 September to 31 August (the academic year). The discount rate for the academic year 2026/27 is 2%. Further information on how to join the Scheme may be obtained from the Bursar, bursar@aldro.org.
Armed Forces and FCDO
Armed Forces and FCDO: Eligible Military families in receipt of the Continuity of Education Allowance (CEA) for their full boarding children will pay 10% of the full boarding fee in addition to the CEA allowance. Day children of serving Military personnel and FCDO families not in receipt of CEA are granted a 20% reduction in day fees (excluding extras).
Clergy
A discount of 20% off day fees is available to those in full-time Christian ministry (excluding extras).
Siblings
When three children attend simultaneously a sibling discount of 20% off day fees for the youngest child will be applicable (excluding extras) whilst all three are in attendance.
Staff
A discount is available for current members of staff. Staff may also be eligible for a mean-tested bursary if they are not able to afford the residual fees after a staff discount has been applied.
Bursaries
The Governors of Aldro are committed to broad access to the school by offering to eligible parents, means-tested financial support with the payment of school fees. Such support may be awarded in the form of a discount of up to 100% on tuition fees payable, depending on the financial, compassionate or other pertinent circumstances of applicants. Bursary awards are subject to repeat testing of parental means each year and may be varied upwards or downwards, depending on parental circumstances.
In addition to the School’s bursary fund, there are a number of educational and charitable trusts which provide assistance with tuition fees. In the majority of cases, these are to assist children who are already attending a fee paying school and due to a change of circumstances may be unable to remain. Aldro School encourages parents/guardians to apply for support where it is felt a good case can be made for assistance. Further information on how to pursue such assistance may be obtained from the Bursar, bursar@aldro.org.

Leavers' Destinations
Impartial & Bespoke
At Aldro we provide impartial and bespoke senior school advice to parents, so they feel confident that their child is heading on to the ‘right’ school. As each child and every school is different, it is hardly surprising that our children have left us to attend 33 different senior schools in the last three years.
This discussion begins with parents in year 5, ensuring that the decision is well-considered and the child is given the best possible preparation. Children therefore head on to a senior school with confidence, where they will thrive and be happy.
This year, 49% of our Form 8s achieved a scholarship to their senior school.
We are fortunate to have built up excellent relationships over a number of years with the top senior schools in the South of England. We regularly send our pupils to a wide range of schools depending on their particular strengths and interests. In recent years, our pupils have gone on to schools including Bradfield, Canford, Charterhouse, Cranleigh, Dean Close, Downe House, Harrow, Lancing, Marlborough, Oundle, Radley, RGS Guildford, Sherborne, Tonbridge, St John’s Leatherhead, Seaford College, St Swithin's, Wellington and Winchester.
"A high proportion of pupils successfully gain scholarships to their chosen senior schools" - ISI Report 2026
Record breaking!
This year, 49% of our Form 8s have achieved a scholarship to their senior school. Senior school scholarships have been offered to Radley, Bradfield, Tonbridge, Charterhouse, Harrow, Lancing, Cranleigh, KESW and Seaford College. Scholarships have been awarded across a broad range of disciplines; academic, sport, drama, music, design & engineering, art, all-rounder and a HM Award. It has been a particularly spectacular year for Miss Allen and her Drama scholars - they are the largest group of drama scholars in Aldro history!
2025 Results
Our 2025 cohort, achieved scholarships across a number of different disciplines; Academic, Art, Drama, Design Engineering, Music and Sport. Our pupils went on to a wide range of senior schools including Charterhouse, Cranleigh School, Dean Close, Harrow, KESW, King's School, Worcester, Lancing College, Marlborough College, Oundle School, Radley College, RGS Guildford, Seaford College, Sherborne Boys, Tonbridge School, Wellington College and Winchester College.

Forms 7 & 8 at Aldro

Drama
Drama at Aldro is fun and uplifting and everyone gets the opportunity to perform.
Each form in years 3-8 has one drama lesson a week in which we aim to develop the children's confidence, self-esteem and drama skills through a range of topics and stimulating exercises.
Children happily throw themselves into a variety of entertaining roles as they improvise, mime, communicate, move, explore pre-existing characters and invent their own.
Drama is an inclusive subject in which group work is key and communication is essential. The pupils make remarkable progress and enter the next stage of their education as confident individuals, competent speakers and in many cases exceptional performers.
School Productions
Forms 3 to 7 are invited to audition for various School Productions and all pupils who wish to take part are welcomed to the stage. We introduce them to vocabulary and practice associated with professional theatre and it is absolutely fundamental that the cast and crew gain a real sense of the enjoyment and excitement that comes from being involved in a production.
These shows are extremely well supported in their production and audiences by family, friends and staff. Recently we have put on memorable performances of High School Musical, The Little Mermaid and Frozen!
Almost 85% of pupils take additional LAMDA lessons
LAMDA
Almost 85% of pupils opt to take additional LAMDA lessons, which are given on a weekly rotational basis. It's a great opportunity for pupils to gain public speaking confidence in a one to one lesson. Students have an opportunity to perform during termly informal showcases and twice yearly examination sessions are held here at Aldro.
Find out more about Rockfest and Music at Aldro
Leavers' Show
During drama lessons and in the weeks following Common Entrance, the Leavers take part in a fabulous range of comedy and drama as they prepare intensely and energetically for a show to mark their time at Aldro.
This is an appropriate moment to reflect on the years they have spent here with us and their contribution to the school. This is a wonderful occasion where the pupils cement their friendships and say farewell to their Prep school in style.
Scholarships
Potential drama scholars are given 1:1 guidance for their audition and performance opportunities. This year, we have achieved an exceptional eight Drama scholarships from Tonbridge, Charterhouse, Harrow, Cranleigh and KESW.
Find out more about Leavers' Destinations

Music
Music is for ALL at Aldro.
Players of all abilities are given the opportunity to take part in making music with others in the many ensembles that rehearse weekly. Big Band, Orchestra, Chapel Choir, Chamber Choir, Training Choir, Junior Choir, Woodwind Ensemble, Brass Ensemble, String Ensemble, Percussion Ensemble, Guitar Ensemble, Brass Band…. there is something for everyone! A ‘give it a go’ attitude permeates throughout the music department at Aldro and the chance to perform on stage in the plethora of concerts is the ultimate reward!
Performances
During the year there are many opportunities for the children to perform from Teatime Concerts, Advanced Musicians Concerts, Termly Concerts, Regatta and of course Aldro's Rockfest in the summer term, where every child has the opportunity to perform a song of their choice, regardless of whether they have additional music lessons. At the last concert performances ranged from Seven Nation Army to Smells Like Teen Spirit - is was a fantastically vibrant event that the children absolutely loved!
More advanced musicians are given opportunities to expand their musical portfolio with regular opportunities to perform and to receive professional feedback from highly regard professional musicians, for example in a performance masterclass with visiting musician Dr Gabby Painter, violinist with Academy St Martin in the Fields.
Music in the classroom
In curriculum lessons, pupils engage in composing, listening, and performing activities that are both stimulating and challenging. Musicians are encouraged to use their instrumental skills within these tasks to develop their creativity and explore through their instruments. Collaboration is key in the music classroom where pupils of all abilities are actively stimulated by one another’s ideas and creations.
We are extremely fortunate to have four choirs at Aldro: a Junior Choir, Training Choir, Chapel Choir and Chamber Choir.
The Junior Choir is for Forms 3 and 4 and is part of the weekly curriculum, Training Choir is an optional activity for children in Forms 5 and 6 and the Chamber Choir is by invitation only to Form 7s and 8s.
The Aldro Chapel Choir is at the heart of every Chapel Service. Formed of auditionees from Form 5 to Form 8, the choir rehearse weekly under the professional leadership of the Director of Music. The choir explore part-singing through a huge range of sacred and secular anthems.
Music Scholars
Pupils are supported, mentored, and encouraged to work towards a music scholarship at their chosen senior school. The Director of Music works closely alongside the team of Visiting Music Teachers to guide pupils through this musical journey. The department has excellent relationships with senior school music departments which helps to guide the preparation for pre-auditions and the scholarship audition itself.

Safeguarding
Aldro recognises its moral and statutory responsibility to safeguard and promote the welfare of all children. Everyone who comes into contact with children and their families has a role to play in this. In order to fulfil this responsibility effectively, everyone should make sure their approach is child centred. This means that they should consider, at all times, what is in the best interests of the child.
At Aldro we make every effort to provide an environment in which children and adults feel safe, secure, valued, respected and confident to talk if they are worried, believing they will be effectively listened to. In recruiting new staff and volunteers, Aldro's safer-recruitment procedures, including conducting all necessary checks, seek to ensure that all school staff are safe to work with children.
Aldro has a Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy to provide staff, volunteers and governors with the framework they need in order to keep children safe and secure in our school. The policy also informs parents and carers how we will safeguard their children whilst they are in our care.

Visit us
Choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions that you will ever make.
We are delighted that you are considering Aldro for your child and we are here to advise and support you – we look forward to welcoming you either through one of our Open Mornings or an individual appointment or a combination of both.
Open Mornings take place every term and provide a fabulous opportunity to visit the school with the whole family, enabling prospective parents and pupils to see for themselves what makes Aldro so special.

Art
The art room at Aldro is a hub of activity every week. Children in all year groups have one hour of art each week to try a number of styles, mediums and techniques.
In addition, there are two enrichment sessions, giving children an opportunity to explore their creativity beyond the curriculum. The activities within these sessions vary every term. Recent popular classes have explored drypoint etchings using recycled CDs, rendering popular artworks in Hama Beads, mini book-making, embroidery, mindful Mandala drawing and learning how to draw paisley patterns.
On Monday afternoons, children who are preparing for Art Scholarship attend a masterclass, which helps them to develop a dynamic and interesting portfolio of art, with a comprehensive sketchbook to support their work. On Thursday afternoons, pupils are able to attend an art masterclass, extending their skills and exploring their independent creativity.
Our aim is to broaden children’s experience of a wide range of materials, media and techniques, including graphics, painting, printing, textiles, mixed media.
Sketchbooks
Pupils are given A4 soft cover sketchbooks in Form Three. Sketchbooks are kept from one Form to the next and replaced as they are filled. Pupils are encouraged to use their sketchbooks to sketch as well as to explore ideas and experiment with techniques. They are also used to collect visual information and inspiration. Pupils are encouraged to see their sketchbooks as a personal space to explore their creativity; they are not marked by the teacher but they are monitored on an individual level and encouragement and guidance are given.
Digital Portfolios
In Forms 6, 7 and 8, pupils take full advantage of their personal laptops, keeping digital portfolios on Teams. They record progress regularly and photograph their final masterpieces. They also use this platform to review and reflect on their work.
We enable children to record from first-hand experience and from imagination, and to select their own ideas to use in their work
Drawing is the foundation of most projects. Pupils are encouraged to draw from direct observation as well as from their imagination. They experience a variety of drawing surfaces and a broad range of drawing media, different scales. They draw for different purposes, for example to explore ideas, to explain ideas to themselves and others, to record information about what they have observed.
The department benefits from a large printing press and pupils explore relief and intaglio printing techniques, such a lino, collagraph and dry-point etching, printing on paper and fabric.
Children paint with a variety of water-based media, such a gouache, watercolours and ready mixed tempera, as well as acrylic paints, in the upper years. All these media are available in the Double Primary System, encouraging pupils to learn to mix their own colours accurately and consistently.
Aldro boasts 2 kilns, allowing pupils to explore a range of ceramic techniques, including coil and slab building, pinch pots and free form sculpture. They learn about the Health and Safety surrounding the use of clay and glazes. Their work is bisque fired and either glazed and fired again, or painted and varnished.
Children in Form 8 design and paint silk ties, which they wear with pride towards the end of the year. Boys and girls are equally enthusiastic about this project, which incorporates study of the history of Sericulture (silk farming) and the welfare issues surrounding the cultivation of silkworms for silk production.
We foster an enjoyment and appreciation of the visual arts and a knowledge of artists, craftspeople and designers.

Exhibitions and competitions
Aldro’s Celebration of Art competition is always a very memorable event which is open to Aldro children and to local schools in the community. It’s a fantastic opportunity for the school’s budding artists to have their work displayed in a public exhibition for visitors to admire, in a transformed ASC! It’s always wonderful to see so much Aldro artwork on display and so many pupils awarded prizes for their efforts. The prize giving ceremony is an evening event, allowing artists to invite friends and family to attend and celebrate their achievements.
We also hold regular holiday art challenges, like the Post-it Note art challenge and the Medical Room Art challenge.
We aim to increase critical awareness of the roles and purposes of art and design in different times and cultures.
Scholarships
For those with artistic flair, there is a well-established programme of support for art scholars. In recent years, Aldro graduates have achieved art scholarships to Harrow, Radley, Charterhouse, Abingdon and Cranleigh.

Our vision and values
Aldro was founded in 1898 and moved to Shackleford from Eastbourne in 1940. We are fortunate to occupy a beautiful setting in the Surrey countryside, and to enjoy the use of some outstanding facilities for a prep school. The ethos of the school is centred on our Christian foundation and priority is given to the highest standards of pastoral care and to the education of the "whole child" as an individual. We encourage our pupils to become caring, thoughtful, and confident members of the school community and to be fully prepared to move on and thrive at their senior schools.
Aldro seeks to be an inclusive school, with a genuine 'family-feel', offering opportunities for all pupils to discover their talents and gifts whilst, encouraging them to strive for excellence. Boarding is a great strength of Aldro, contributing to the busy and vibrant atmosphere here and teaching the pupils vital skills of independence and responsibility which stand them in good stead for their future schools.
To provide an outstanding and broad education for all pupils that will instil in them a life-long love of learning and make them positive contributors to society.
